LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION: COMMA QUESTION MARKS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation: Comma Question Marks
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation: Comma Question Marks, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we punctuate written work? 2. How do we use these punctuation marks: comma and full stop?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation: Comma Question Marks together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: Communication and self-expression as learners make coherent sentences and paragraphs featuring the comma and

question marks

• Digital literacy: interacting with digital technology as learner use digital devices to type sentences and text, access and play online and offline

games.

Values:
Love: sharing as learners, in pairs take punctuation cards with different punctuation marks and match them with their names.

Link to other subjects:

Learner is able to link the concept of punctuation marks to their learning in other learning areas.
